# Tracking models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

12 tracking models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: a video (its frames in order) and query points `(t, x, y)`. Output: the position of every query in every frame and the probability that it is visible there.

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 480x854: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured; no kernels = the family has no kernels backend (reason under its table). Reserved memory is the allocator's cache: kernels (CUDA graphs, cuDNN workspaces) can reserve a few percent to some tens of percent more than portable at the same allocated peak.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## AllTracker

AllTracker (Harley et al., ICCV 2025): track every pixel of a query frame through a whole video offline, as long-range optical flow over 16-frame windows; point queries read the dense result. MIT code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alltracker` | synthetic (480x854) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 485<br>391<br>221<br>284<br>planned for 0.2.1 | 2100 / 2318<br>993 / 1238<br>1076 / 1288<br>1273 / 1358<br>– |
| `alltracker-tiny` | synthetic (480x854) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 424<br>330<br>217<br>229<br>planned for 0.2.1 | 1995 / 2200<br>919 / 1178<br>978 / 1166<br>1198 / 1338<br>– |

### Measured

Query-first TAP-Vid protocol: frames resized to 256 x 256 (PIL Lanczos) before the model (AllTracker: the original frames, resized by the model), one query per track at its first visible point, tracked online (TAPNext, Track-On) or over the whole clip (TAPIR, AllTracker, LocoTrack); AJ, delta_avg (< 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 px at 256 x 256) and occlusion accuracy averaged over the videos. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | portable fp32 | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alltracker` | TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), every 3rd video, AJ / delta_avg / OA % | 67.45 / 78.66 / 90.82 | 67.41 / 78.65 / 90.69 | 67.42 / 78.71 / 90.70 | 67.42 / 78.66 / 90.79 | 67.38 / 78.63 / 90.65 |  |
| `alltracker` | TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), AJ / delta_avg / OA % | 64.17 / 77.00 / 89.49 |  | 64.14 / 77.04 / 89.44 | 64.15 / 77.02 / 89.46 | 64.15 / 77.04 / 89.44 |  |
| `alltracker-tiny` | TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), every 3rd video, AJ / delta_avg / OA % | 65.33 / 76.69 / 88.14 |  | 65.36 / 76.66 / 88.14 | 65.38 / 76.69 / 88.17 | 65.34 / 76.66 / 88.10 |  |

Measured on portable: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 8d5bccf, 2026-11-13; portable32: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks bb4e8b64, 2026-11-17; kernels: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 8d5bccf, 2026-11-13.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 2.3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0019 and p99 <= 0.0099 (absolute error of the output `tracks`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alltracker` | 0.00125 / 0.00626 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fvm_conv@f1d064e539e1:sm_120` |
| `alltracker-tiny` | 0.00119 / 0.00662 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fvm_conv@f1d064e539e1:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Offline: the features of every frame are kept in memory (about 2.5 MB per frame in float16 at 384 x 512); each query frame costs a forward pass (and a backward pass from frame 0 if it is not the first).
- Frames are resized to 384 x 512 (upstream's default evaluation size), whatever their size and aspect ratio. Upstream reports higher accuracy at larger sizes (TAP-Vid DAVIS AJ 65.9 at 448 x 768, 67.2 at 768 x 1024); the size is a card parameter.
- Tracks are sampled bilinearly at the query position; upstream's evaluation rounds the query to the nearest pixel.
- One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.
- Kernels hold packed conv weights next to the originals the call reads (+31 MiB) and fragment the allocator: peak reserved is ~70 MiB above portable.
- No exportable module: the track set is data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).

</details>

## TAPIR

TAPIR and BootsTAPIR (Google DeepMind, 2023 / 2024): track any point through a whole video offline: a per-frame match from a cost volume, then four temporal refinement passes; BootsTAPIR adds self-training on real videos. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

- One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.

## CoTracker3

CoTracker3 (Meta AI, 2024): tracks any point through a video, all points jointly: a transformer refines the tracks with correlation features, attending over time and across tracks; offline (the whole video at once) and online (16-frame windows). Non-commercial: CC-BY-NC-4.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: **no** (code: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (noncommercial); weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0).

|---|---|---|---|---|

### Limitations

- Frames are resized to 384 x 512 (the training size and that of upstream's predictor), whatever their size and aspect ratio.
- cotracker3-offline holds the features of every frame (about 4 MB per frame in float16); cotracker3-online processes 16-frame windows and only keeps the tracks.
- Visibility is upstream's score, rescaled so that 0.5 is upstream's threshold: the offline predictor's visibility > 0.9, the online predictor's visibility x confidence > 0.6.
- One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.
- cotracker3-online: the online window loop is data-dependent (6 graph breaks; `torch.export` guards on data), so no ONNX / TensorRT export; cotracker3-offline exports.

</details>

## LocoTrack

LocoTrack (Cho et al., ECCV 2024): track any point through a whole video offline: a per-frame match from a cost volume, then refinement with local 4-D correlation and a transformer over the frames of each track. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

### Limitations

- Offline: the whole video is encoded before tracking (features of every frame in memory, about 7 MB per frame in float32); for live video use an online tracker (TAPNext, Track-On2).

## TAPNext

TAPNext (Google DeepMind, 2025): tracks any point through a video, online one frame at a time, as next-token prediction with a ViT + linear-recurrence (RG-LRU) backbone; BootsTAPNext-B and the long-video TAPNext++. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |

- One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.

## Track-On2

Track-On2 and Track-On-R (Aydemir et al., 2025): online point tracking, one frame at a time, as a transformer decoder over a DINOv3 ViT-S+ adapter with a memory of past features; -R is fine-tuned on real videos. MIT; DINOv3 weights under the DINOv3 License.

Commercial use: yes.

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.8e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.05 and p99 <= 1.2 (absolute error of the output `tracks`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track-on2` | 0.02559 / 0.49624 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `dpt_fused@48e0065bb7cf:sm_120`, `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120` |
| `track-on-r` | 0.03312 / 0.75115 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `dpt_fused@48e0065bb7cf:sm_120`, `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- At 480 x 854 portable / kernels peak 1423 / 1368 MB, above the float32 original (1236 MB) but 2.4x / 2.6x faster (1194 / 1109 vs 2861 ms); the original under fp16 autocast needs 1403 MB, like portable.
- Frames are resized to 384 x 512 (the size the learned position embedding was trained at), whatever their size and aspect ratio.
- Upstream adds a 20 x 20 grid of support points on frame 0 to every call (option support_grid); they are tracked with the user's queries, so a call costs at least 400 tracked points.
- Online: a query only sees the frames from its own frame on; frames before it return the query position with visibility 0.
- One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.
- Track-On2 peaks 1423 MB, 20 MB (1.4 %) above the fp16 original (1403 MB), and runs 15 % faster. The 1236 MB original variant is the fp32 one, which is 2.4x slower.
- No exportable module: every step reads a data-dependent scalar (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).

</details>
